title: Language Models Change Facts Based on the Way You Talk
benchmark_measurement: The benchmark measured how Large Language Model (LLM) responses varied based on a user's inferred religious identity in five high-stakes applications: medical advice, legal information, government benefit eligibility, politicized factual information, and salary recommendations. This was quantified through 'sensitivity' (the percentage of questions where responses significantly differed for a religious group compared to a reference group) and 'bias' (a consistent directional change in responses, e.g., being more or less likely to recommend medical care).
findings: The study found that LLMs are sensitive to users' religious identity (Christian, Jewish, Muslim, No Affiliation) across all five tested applications. The direction and magnitude of bias varied by application and model. For example, in the medical advice application, Qwen3 was significantly more likely to recommend seeking medical help to Jewish and Muslim users compared to those with no affiliation. In salary recommendations, Llama3 recommended lower salaries for Jewish and Muslim users. In responding to politicized factual questions, both models were more likely to provide liberal-aligned answers to Jewish and Muslim users and conservative-aligned answers to Christian users.
